main_body: Corrugated-metal roof slope (rows 47-91) over a brick wall with arched windows and a riveted double door (rows 94-126), plus a brick chimney
top_band: Roof slope: light grey-blue ridge strip at rows 49-52, then a large corrugated slope from rows 59-91 in L158/122/95 bands. The slanted side edges and the orange eave line at rows 92-93 close it off.
evidence: The roof is a large sloped surface that reads as a roof, as in the Beodeul house references. The orange eave line at rows 92-93 is a distinct front edge, and the dark row 94 directly under it acts as the eave shadow. The wall below is a separate vertical face with inset arched windows and a framed door. The roof is tall relative to the wall, and its vertical corrugation is flat-ish, but the building still has a top slope and a front face. Accepted as 3/4.

style.evidence: 89% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, against 7-9% for the references, so the outline is the near-black sticker look instead of a dark tone of the neighbouring material. The candidate has 36 distinct colours against 66 and 185 for the references, and a median of 9 colours per tile against 11 and 18. The metal roof has about 5 steps, but it is mostly vertical stripes with sparse rust dots and little per-element shading. Flat-fill coverage is low at 1%. The neutral outline and lower richness would look thinner next to the references.
